observation.visible_scene: A low-light, blue-gray jungle canopy shrouded in heavy mist. A dense, sloping wall of fern-like palm fronds fills the right side and lower center of the frame; two taller, slender palm-like trees stand silhouetted near the middle against a pale foggy sky; the entire left half is open, swirling haze with no distinct objects.
visible_changes: The mist on the left continuously drifts and swirls, its density and shape changing from frame to frame (patches thicken and thin, edges shift) without revealing or hiding any fixed object.

The fronds of the right-side vegetation mass and the crowns of the two central trees sway and deform subtly, consistent with wind, while their overall positions in the frame stay essentially unchanged.

Faint diagonal streaks (suggestive of falling rain or drifting mist wisps) appear intermittently in the upper sky area across several frames (e.g., around 0.56s, 0.64s, 1.52s, 2.0s, 2.4s, 2.88s) and fade in others.

The scene composition (placement of the central trees and the right fern wall relative to the frame edges) remains stable throughout, indicating the camera is largely stationary with at most negligible drift.
No object enters or exits the frame; the visible process is the ongoing atmospheric motion (fog movement and foliage sway) rather than any discrete event.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the fog/mist and whether precipitation is actually occurring beyond the visible streaks.
What lies in the obscured left region and below the canopy.
The time of day and weather context before and after this cropped segment.
uncertain_details: Whether the diagonal sky streaks are rain, mist wisps, lens/compression artifacts, or transient lighting.
Whether there is any slight camera movement versus purely static framing, since the background evidence is low-contrast.
The exact direction and strength of the wind causing the frond sway.
